title: Anthropic founders secure control as Nvidia ousts Jensen Huang
excerpt: Anthropic's founders have locked in voting control, making them harder to oust. Nvidia's Jensen Huang didn't have that protection.
content_html:
Anthropic's founders have a safeguard Jensen Huang never had

By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

Author of the AI Insider newsletter

2026-11-20T15:11:51.219Z

I bet Jensen Huang wishes he'd thought of this.

Anthropic's founders have devised an ingenious way to make sure they don't suffer the same fate as Nvidia's ousted CEO: Give themselves control of the company.

I've seen this movie before.

In 2004, I covered Google's IPO for MarketWatch. Cofounders Larry Page and Sergey Brin insisted their search engine was so important to the world that they needed special voting stock to protect their mission.

It worked. They retained control, and other tech founders, including Mark Zuckerberg, followed their lead.

Now Anthropic is taking this idea even further.

Its seven cofounders, including CEO Dario Amodei, collectively control 50.1% of shareholder votes through a special Class F share. No matter how many ordinary shares Anthropic sells, that voting power remains intact.

A separate, independent trust, established to protect Anthropic's AI safety mission, holds Class T stock that generally lets it appoint and remove a majority of the board.

Anthropic says these protections are necessary because AI is so powerful that its development must be shielded from short-term investor pressure.

There's a more practical benefit: It's extremely difficult to oust leaders who control their company's voting power.

Which brings me back to Jensen.

He cofounded Nvidia 33 years ago, when it made video game chips. Back then, special voting stock was rare in tech. And claiming video games were too important to humanity to leave to ordinary shareholders would have been a tough sell.

Today, Nvidia powers the AI revolution. But Huang owns only about 3.5% of its shares, without special voting rights.

His board pushed him out. His supporters want him back.

I suspect Jensen would do things differently if he could start again.
